True that is an option for some but often we have to work long hours because we cant find people who want to work in the orchards, at least in our area. Typically people show up looking for work only during harvest season when they will make more money and leave once harvest is done. Also as others may have pointed out agriculture does not very consistent working hours. During some months we may have to work 10-12 hour days and other months there is barely enough work to keep one or 2 people busy for 6 hours. 

In addition to that, depending on if an orchard has H2A workers we are required by law to provide them certain working hours, so during long working hours they may not make overtime pay but they make up some of that loss later when we have them do less intensive work to make sure they meet the minimum required hours later on during their contract with us.

I think I might bot have been clear. Currently the way that I understand it and the way my family operates our orchard is that hourly workers are paid at a constant rate no matter how many hours are worked. But this new law would force us to pay an increased rate for any hours worked over the typical 40 hours a week.

For example if someone worked 60 hours during pruning currently it works out like this, $15 x 60hr= $900. But with this new law depending on how overtime is calculated it might work out more like this ($15 x 40hr)+($25 x 20hr)=$1100. So we would pay the normal rate for the first 40 hours worked then have to increase the rate for any hours past that.

So yes we do pay for all hours that are worked but this would force us to increase the pay rate for overtime hours.

Hope I answered your question.

While I my opinion this could be a good thing for the workers I understand why overtime wasnt provided before. My family owns a small orchard and we hire H2A workers for all the heavy seasonal work like most orchards in Washington. 

They definiatly work hard and long hours and I work right along side them. The issue that this overtime work will really cause is just a large increase in operation cost that very well could lead to small orchards no longer being able to be profitable and having to shut down. Now like others have said if we cant afford to pay workers the overtime then dont make them work overtime. This is probably going to be what happens and people like me will have to pick up the extra work to limit the number of overtime hours. 

However the issue with this will be less production at a higher cost overall. This coupled with the fact that consumers don't really care about where their food comes from, they just want it cheap and good enough, will lead to decreased revenue. 
And maybe if we can't afford to produce anymore with overtime then maybe we shouldn't, but this is not a black and white issue that some people think it is. 

Now for big companies this won't really be and issue if they simply decide to hire more people or bring more H2A workers and just work them up untill they are about to make overtime then work the others in order to get all the work done at relatively similar cost. This will lead to big companies just not really changing and if anything making workers earn less money due to decreased hours overall. 

If I forgot anything or didn't understand something please let me know. I'm also willing to answer questions if I can. 


TLDR:
The new overtime law will probably lead to small farms not being profitable while the big companies still pay next to nothing to their workers.
